name: proof-too-large
spec: op-private-interop/docs/DESIGN.md: the claim is an ordinary L2 transaction, and it leads the range it describes.
description: A well-formed claim whose proof slot is MaxProofSize + 1 bytes — the smallest violation there is. Everything about it is canonical; the only thing wrong is that it is too big, which is why the case has to carry the real bytes rather than an over-declared length. The proof is all zeroes so the fixture compresses to nothing. Refused by Encode as well as Decode: a producer that can emit what its own decoder rejects will do it at the worst possible time.
